newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.09 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.09 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real closed at 1.0219 per dollar, down 0.09 percent, in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.022 to 1.027 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new real-dollar mini-band in an afternoon auction. The previous mini-band, set on Sept 30, was between 1.021 and 1.026 reais to the dollar.
After opening at 1.0216, the real fell to 1.0223 on dollar outflows and speculation over a possible drop in the mini-band, dealers said.
In the afternoon, trade was calm due to some dollar inflows and the Central Bank's changing of the mini-band, which stopped speculation and led to dollar selling, they added.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.07 percent to end at 1.0274 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.041 per greenback, up 0.1 percent, traders said.
